---
title: "A supervision, authorship or collaboration problem feels stuck"
last-reviewed: "2026-08-28"
---

## Separate disagreement from harm

Start by describing the problem. Are expectations unclear, is an agreed task repeatedly missed, or do you disagree about contribution? If coercion or unsafe behaviour is involved, seek independent support before trying to negotiate directly.

## Try this now

1. Preserve factual dated records and relevant agreements.
2. Identify what needs deciding, who can decide it and which agreement or standard applies.
3. Describe each position fairly.
4. Suggest a specific resolution and a date to check whether it has helped.
5. Seek independent advice when authority or power makes direct resolution unsafe.
6. Keep sensitive details in the authorised confidential process.

## What to take when asking

Bring the relevant agreements, contribution records and messages. Explain the effect on your work, what you've tried and what decision or protection you need.

## Stop or escalate

Use independent formal routes for bullying, harassment, discrimination, retaliation, authorship coercion, suspected misconduct or conflicts of interest. Do not rely only on a person implicated in the concern.

## You are moving again when

The agreed roles and actions are recorded, any necessary protection or review is underway, and the authorship or project records reflect the decision.

Use the [authorship record](../templates/authorship-conversation.qmd) and [escalation builder](../templates/escalation-message.qmd).
